network.overall_strategy: An acetone-centered surface cyanosulfidic network is used because the supplied literature supports valine formation there most strongly. The experimentally anchored core is the Patel et al. sequence acetone -> acetone cyanohydrin -> thioamide -> branched hydroxynitrile -> aminonitrile -> valine under HCN/H2S/Cu conditions in anoxic surface pools. To reach ten distinct routes without invoking the unresolved C6 chain-shortening branch, the network adds a plausible upstream triose entry through glyceraldehyde and a chemically standard alternative terminal hydrolysis via valinamide. Explicit sulfur and water bookkeeping is written into the balanced reactions. The target is valine without specified chirality because the reviewed prebiotic chemistry does not resolve homochirality.

reactions.name: Triose isomerization of glyceraldehyde to dihydroxyacetone

conditions.other: Anoxic surface carbonyl pool undergoing wet-dry concentration; near-neutral to mildly basic aqueous intervals.

reactions.mechanism: Aldose-ketose isomerization through an enediol or related tautomeric intermediate.
reactions.reasoning: Speculative upstream entry. Triose aldose-ketose interconversion is chemically routine and provides a plausible source of dihydroxyacetone feeding the Patel valine chemistry. The curated review does not report this as a valine-specific experimental step, so it is included only as a plausible pre-entry to the documented cyanosulfidic network (Patel et al., 2015; speculative).

reactions.name: Partial Cu/H2S-mediated reductive deoxygenation of dihydroxyacetone to hydroxyacetone

conditions.other: Anoxic cyanosulfidic evaporitic or geothermal pool; dissolved or suspended Cu supplied from weathered copper minerals; balanced graph implicitly uses multiple sulfide equivalents.

reactions.mechanism: Copper-assisted partial reductive removal of one terminal hydroxymethyl oxygen equivalent, with sulfide serving as reductant and being oxidized to disulfane.
reactions.reasoning: Speculative partial deoxygenation. Patel et al. (2015) demonstrate Cu/H2S reduction of dihydroxyacetone toward acetone; isolating hydroxyacetone as a partially reduced stage is chemically plausible but not explicitly reported in the supplied valine study. Disulfane is written as a sulfur-redox bookkeeping product under anoxic cyanosulfidic conditions (Patel et al., 2015; speculative).

reactions.name: Cu/H2S-mediated reductive deoxygenation of dihydroxyacetone to acetone

conditions.other: Anoxic cyanosulfidic pool; wet-dry concentration; balanced graph implicitly uses multiple H2S and H2S2 equivalents.

reactions.mechanism: Net copper-assisted reductive deoxygenation of the triose-derived substrate to the C3 ketone acetone.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) experimentally support the dihydroxyacetone-to-acetone entry under surface cyanosulfidic conditions. H2S2 and H2O are written explicitly here to satisfy mass balance and to reflect sulfide oxidation during Cu/H2S-mediated reduction; the exact sulfur speciation for this deoxygenation is not fully resolved in the review, but the overall transformation is supported (Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Cu/H2S-mediated reductive deoxygenation of hydroxyacetone to acetone

conditions.other: Anoxic cyanosulfidic pool; hydroxyacetone available directly or from upstream sugar chemistry; balanced graph implicitly uses multiple sulfide equivalents.

reactions.mechanism: Copper-assisted reductive removal of the hydroxymethyl oxygen from hydroxyacetone to give acetone.
reactions.reasoning: This is the alternative upstream entry reported in the reviewed cyanosulfidic valine chemistry. Patel et al. (2015) describe hydroxyacetone reduction to acetone under Cu/H2S conditions. As in rxn_003, H2S2 is made explicit here as conservative sulfur-redox bookkeeping rather than a uniquely established sulfur sink for this specific step (Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Cyanohydrin formation from acetone

conditions.other: Cyanide-rich anoxic surface pool; concentration enhanced during evaporation.

reactions.mechanism: Nucleophilic addition of cyanide to the ketone carbonyl followed by protonation of the alkoxide.
reactions.reasoning: Directly supported in the Patel cyanosulfidic network: cyanide adds to acetone to give the tertiary cyanohydrin that seeds valine carbon-skeleton construction (Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Thioamide formation from acetone cyanohydrin

conditions.other: Sulfide-rich cyanosulfidic pool under anoxic surface conditions.

reactions.mechanism: Hydrogen sulfide adds across the nitrile and tautomerizes to the thioamide.
reactions.reasoning: Directly supported nitrile-to-thioamide conversion by H2S addition, a key activating move in the cyanosulfidic framework for downstream reductive chemistry (Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Cu/H2S-mediated chain extension of the thioamide with HCN

conditions.other: Anoxic Cu/H2S redox chemistry in a cyanosulfidic pool; likely bottleneck; balanced graph implicitly uses multiple H2S and H2S2 equivalents.

reactions.mechanism: Copper-mediated reductive rearrangement and homologation of the thioamide with HCN to give the branched C5 alpha-hydroxynitrile.
reactions.reasoning: This is the key C-C bond-forming homologation of the reviewed valine route. Patel et al. (2015) support Cu/H2S-mediated rearrangement of the thioamide with HCN to the branched C5 hydroxynitrile. The detailed radical or polar mechanism remains an open question in the review, so the balanced form shown here should be read as a stoichiometrically explicit representation of an experimentally motivated but mechanistically complex step. Disulfane is retained explicitly because the curated review identifies H2S2 as a sulfur-oxidation byproduct in this chemistry (Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Strecker-type amination of the branched hydroxynitrile

conditions.other: Ammonia-rich rehydration interval in an anoxic surface pool.

reactions.mechanism: Ammonolysis or substitution at the alpha-carbon replaces hydroxyl by amino and releases water.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) describe conversion of the alpha-hydroxynitrile to the aminonitrile with ammonia. Writing water explicitly makes the substitution mass-balanced and identifies the direct aminonitrile precursor to valine (Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Net hydrolysis of valine aminonitrile to valine

conditions.other: Prolonged aqueous heating during geothermal cycling; graph encodes the net two-water hydrolysis without repeating molecule IDs.

reactions.mechanism: Overall nitrile hydration through an amide stage to the amino acid carboxylate.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) support overall hydrolysis of valine aminonitrile to valine. The graph lists water once, but the balanced net transformation uses two waters and releases ammonia. No chiral enrichment step is included, so this node represents valine without specified enantiomeric excess (Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Partial hydrolysis of valine aminonitrile to valinamide

conditions.other: Early-stage nitrile hydrolysis during aqueous rehydration in an anoxic pool.

reactions.mechanism: First hydration of the nitrile to the corresponding primary amide.
reactions.reasoning: Speculative subdivision of the overall Patel hydrolysis. Amide intermediates are standard in nitrile hydrolysis, so valinamide is a chemically conservative intermediate even though the supplied review does not isolate it as a valine-specific node. It is included here to represent an alternative terminal resolution of the same aminonitrile pool (Patel et al., 2015; speculative).

reactions.name: Hydrolysis of valinamide to valine

conditions.other: Continued aqueous heating or repeated wet-dry cycles in an anoxic surface pool.

reactions.mechanism: Hydrolysis of the primary amide to the carboxylic acid with ammonia release.
reactions.reasoning: Speculative completion of the stepwise hydrolysis route. Conversion of valinamide to valine with ammonia release is chemically standard and consistent with the net hydrolysis reported by Patel et al. (2015), but it is not separately demonstrated in the supplied valine review (Patel et al., 2015; speculative).

pathways.name: Glyceraldehyde entry with direct DHA-to-acetone reduction and net hydrolysis
pathways.description: Glyceraldehyde first isomerizes to dihydroxyacetone, which is reduced directly to acetone before entering the literature-supported cyanohydrin-thioamide-hydroxynitrile-aminonitrile sequence and net hydrolysis to valine.

pathways.description: As in P1, but the terminal nitrile hydrolysis is expanded into a stepwise valinamide route before valine formation.

pathways.name: Glyceraldehyde entry with stepwise DHA-to-hydroxyacetone-to-acetone reduction and net hydrolysis
pathways.description: Glyceraldehyde isomerizes to dihydroxyacetone, passes through the speculative partially reduced hydroxyacetone stage, then converges on acetone and the documented cyanosulfidic valine core before net hydrolysis to valine.

pathways.name: Glyceraldehyde entry with stepwise upstream reduction and valinamide resolution
pathways.description: This route follows the same glyceraldehyde to hydroxyacetone to acetone branch as P3, but uses the stepwise amide route for the final nitrile hydrolysis.

pathways.name: Dihydroxyacetone direct entry with net hydrolysis
pathways.description: Dihydroxyacetone enters directly into the documented Cu/H2S reduction to acetone and then follows the canonical cyanosulfidic sequence to valine by net hydrolysis.

pathways.name: Dihydroxyacetone direct entry with valinamide resolution
pathways.description: Dihydroxyacetone feeds the same acetone-centered core as P5, but the aminonitrile is hydrolyzed stepwise through valinamide.

pathways.name: Hydroxyacetone direct entry with net hydrolysis
pathways.description: Hydroxyacetone enters directly through the literature-supported Cu/H2S deoxygenation to acetone and then proceeds through the Patel valine core to net hydrolysis.

pathways.name: Hydroxyacetone direct entry with valinamide resolution
pathways.description: Hydroxyacetone converges on acetone as in P7, but the terminal nitrile hydrolysis is resolved through valinamide.

pathways.name: Acetone hub entry with net hydrolysis
pathways.description: When acetone is already available in the surface carbonyl pool, valine can arise by direct entry into the cyanohydrin-thioamide-hydroxynitrile-aminonitrile sequence followed by net hydrolysis.

pathways.name: Acetone hub entry with valinamide resolution
pathways.description: Direct acetone entry again follows the Patel core, but the final hydrolysis is encoded stepwise through valinamide before valine appears.

evaluation.network_feedback: Connected 15-molecule, 11-reaction network with no conservation failures under the supplied RDKit check and a strong Patel et al. 2015 cyanosulfidic core. The best-supported route is P5, which follows DHA -> acetone -> acetone cyanohydrin -> thioamide -> branched hydroxynitrile -> aminonitrile -> valine and avoids the unresolved C6 chain-shortening branch. The network should still be tightened by writing the balanceable reactions explicitly: rxn_002 = mol_006 + 2 mol_003 -> mol_007 + mol_001 + mol_015; rxn_003 = mol_006 + 4 mol_003 -> mol_008 + 2 mol_001 + 2 mol_015; rxn_004 = mol_007 + 2 mol_003 -> mol_008 + mol_001 + mol_015; rxn_007 = mol_010 + mol_002 + 3 mol_003 -> mol_011 + mol_004 + 2 mol_015; rxn_009 = mol_012 + 2 mol_001 -> mol_014 + mol_004. Main residual uncertainties are the less directly evidenced rxn_001 and rxn_002, the optional valinamide branch rxn_010-rxn_011, and the absence of explicit Cu and pH annotations at the reaction level. Target achievement is strong, and leaving valine achiral is appropriate for the racemic literature context.
